turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hi, thanks for coming in today. What's been going on for you lately?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It's been... fine, I guess. Just a lot of stress at work and I've been running behind on errands. Nothing that's really bothering me. (pauses briefly) Just trying to stay on top of things, you know?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I do. Yes, I do. It can be really hard to prioritize tasks and keep up with everything, especially when work stress is piling up. What do you think is causing the stress at work?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It's just... a lot of pressure to meet deadlines, and I've been putting off some things that I need to do. I don't know, it's just feeling a bit overwhelming. (gets slightly defensive) I'm managing, though. I'm not losing sleep over it or anything.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That's good to hear. It's understandable that you're feeling a bit overwhelmed. It's okay to take some time for yourself and prioritize things that are important to you. Have you considered talking to a supervisor or someone at work about your stress levels? It might be helpful to have someone there to support you and help you prioritize things better.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (pauses, seeming slightly uncomfortable) I don't know... I'm not really sure that would help, to be honest. I just need to find a way to get everything done on my own, I guess. (quickly adds) But thanks for offering.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's okay. I understand. Sometimes it can be hard to talk to someone else about our struggles, especially if it's work-related. It's important to take care of yourself and ask for help when you need it. It might be helpful to take a break and do something fun for yourself, like going for a walk or doing something you enjoy. It can help clear your mind and give you some perspective on things. Do you have any hobbies or interests that you enjoy doing?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (sighs) Yeah, I used to like hiking, but it's been a while since I've had time for that. And lately, I've just been too tired after work to do much of anything. (pauses, seeming a bit disconnected) I don't know, it's just hard to get motivated lately.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It can be difficult to find motivation when we're feeling stressed and overwhelmed. It's okay to take some time for yourself and find ways to relax and recharge. Have you tried anything to help with your stress levels?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (shrugs slightly) I've tried... stuff. I mean, I've been exercising more, trying to get some more sleep. But it's not like it's really making a difference. (pauses, looking a bit frustrated) I just feel like no matter what I do, I'm still going to be running behind and feeling anxious all the time.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's okay. It's understandable that you're feeling frustrated. It can be hard to find ways to relax and get things done, especially when we're feeling overwhelmed. Sometimes, it might be helpful to try some new things and see if they make a difference. For example, some people find it helpful to try journaling or meditation to help with their stress levels. It might be worth trying those out and see if they help you feel better.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (scoffs slightly) Journaling? Meditation? I don't know... I'm not really the type to do that sort of thing. I just need to find a way to get my head on straight and stop worrying about everything, you know? (pauses, seeming a bit annoyed) Can we talk about something else?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Of course. What else would you like to talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (pauses, seeming to consider) I don't know... I just feel like I'm always on edge now. I'll be getting ready to leave the house, and suddenly I'll think of something I need to do before I can actually go. It's just... (trails off, seeming hesitant to continue)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (nodding) Yeah, I understand. It's okay to feel anxious and stressed. It's a normal part of life. It's important to find healthy ways to cope with that stress, but it's okay to feel overwhelmed sometimes. It's important to be kind to yourself and give yourself some space to figure things out. Do you think you could talk to someone about how you're feeling? It might be helpful to have someone there to support you and help you figure things out.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looks down, seeming embarrassed) I don't know... I don't want to be one of those people who's always complaining about stuff. I just need to... (pauses, struggling to find the right words) I need to get a handle on this, I guess. But it's just... (trails off, seeming frustrated)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's okay. It's understandable that you're feeling frustrated. It can be hard to find the right words to express how we're feeling. It might be helpful to talk to someone about how you're feeling. They might be able to offer some advice or support that can help you feel better. Would you like me to help you find someone to talk to?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looks up, seeming slightly annoyed) No, it's fine. I don't need any help finding someone to talk to. I just... (pauses, seeming to reconsider) I just need to figure some things out on my own, I guess. (pauses again) I'm sorry, I'm just really tired of feeling like this.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's okay. It's understandable that you're feeling tired of feeling this way. It's okay to feel frustrated and overwhelmed. It's important to take care of yourself and figure things out on your own, but it's also okay to ask for help sometimes. Would you like me to stay with you for a little while and help you think through some of these feelings?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looks down, seeming embarrassed) No, it's okay. Really. I just need to... (pauses, struggling to find the right words) I need to get out of here, I guess. I'll be fine. (starts to get up from the couch)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (nodding) Okay, no problem. I'm glad you feel better. Take care of yourself, okay?
